title: fill
description: `fill(X,Y,C)` creates filled polygonal regions as Patch graphics. Integer coordinate and CData classes remain authoritative on the Patch object; conversion to renderer geometry is an explicit client-side boundary.
behaviors: Equal-length row or column vector X and Y inputs create one region regardless of orientation; matrix inputs create independently addressable regions from columns.
When either coordinate is a matrix, an equal-length coordinate vector matching the matrix row count is shared across every matrix column; square matrices are grouped by columns.
Multiple X,Y,C groups create multiple Patch graphics.
C accepts color text, RGB triples, or numeric indexed color data.
XData, YData, and CData preserve the original numeric class and shape.
A leading axes handle targets an existing axes; typed-integer numeric aliases are available only when RunMat extensions are enabled.

gpu_support.notes: GPU-resident inputs gather exactly through their owning provider and Patch construction executes on the client.

examples.output: h is a Patch graphics handle

examples.description: Use exact integer coordinates and indexed color data
Create one independently addressable Patch per matrix column
examples.output: h is a two-element Patch handle vector; each handle retains its column's typed XData, YData, and CData

faqs.question: Is fill an array-construction function?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB-compatible fill creates Patch graphics. Use createArray to construct constant-valued arrays.
